title: National Museum Cardiff: Masterpieces
subtitle: Twenty paintings connecting Welsh landscapes, occupied interiors and figures with a task.
introduction:
Snow changes the arrangement of a Paris district; a pool of light makes part of Ewenny Priory legible; a tidal shore becomes ground that people and cattle must cross. These works treat a setting as something with conditions. Weather, routes and illumination affect what can happen within it and how much of it can be seen.

The selection also brings that attention indoors and close to individual figures. A painter holds the tools of his profession, children occupy a classroom in different ways, and card players watch one another. Landscape and portraiture meet in the practical question of how a person belongs to a place.
visitNote: The twenty paintings form an editorial selection from the collection. They are not a fixed room list, and individual works may be on loan or in storage. Use Museum Wales’s current collection records and visitor information to check display before travelling.

books.title: Impressionism: A Centenary Exhibition
books.author: Anne Dayez, Michel Hoog and Charles S. Moffett
books.note: The catalogue supplies context for Manet’s snow scene and Renoir’s La Parisienne. Their different uses of a lightly described setting become clearer beside the more detailed landscapes and interiors in this guide.

works.title: Effect of Snow at Petit-Montrouge
works.credit: Édouard Manet. Effect of Snow at Petit-Montrouge. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The snow appears in patches between broad shapes of building rather than as an even covering over a detailed map. A spire helps keep the district identifiable beneath the ochre-grey sky. Manet allows the weather to reorganise the place: distinctions of light and dark become more decisive than an inventory of its architecture.

works.title: Transept of Ewenny Priory
works.credit: J. M. W. Turner. Transept of Ewenny Priory, Glamorganshire. Image credit: J. M. W. Turner. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The church does not disclose all its structure at once. Light catches parts of the screen and floor while upper walls and recesses remain harder to read. Turner gives looking a sequence within the interior. Understanding the building requires passing between illuminated surfaces and what their neighbouring shadows withhold.

works.title: Carneddau Mountains from Pencerrig
works.credit: Thomas Jones. Carneddau Mountains from Pencerrig. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/thomas-jones/carneddau-mountains-from-pencerrig-1776
works.description: Tracks and field divisions keep the slopes attached to human use, even as the view extends toward distant ridges. The museum identifies this as the landscape near Jones’s family home at Pencerrig. That specificity matters: the painting’s ordered distances belong to an encountered place, not merely a generalised idea of mountain scenery.

works.title: Saint Peter
works.credit: El Greco. St. Peter. Image credit: El Greco. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The lifted hand is a second centre beside the pale face. Blue drapery and elongated forms connect them within an otherwise restrained setting of cloud and shadow. The title identifies Saint Peter, but the immediate encounter is built from bodily attention: a turn, an upward tension and a gesture held close to the chest.

works.title: Landscape with Saint Philip Baptizing the Eunuch
works.catalogueTitle: Landscape with St. Philip Baptizing the Eunuch
works.credit: Claude Lorrain. Landscape with St. Philip Baptizing the Eunuch. Image credit: Claude Lorrain; Source credit: Princeton Art Museum. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Proportional resize and JPEG compression; full source frame retained.
works.description: The figures beside the carriage occupy only a small part of the landscape. Tall trees give the baptism a sheltered setting, while the open distance preserves the larger journey around it. Claude does not need to enlarge the event to give it a place; the extensive world continues beyond the travellers’ immediate encounter.

works.title: Hagar and Ishmael in the Wilderness
works.catalogueTitle: Hagar and Ishmael in the Wilderness
works.credit: Andrea Sacchi. Hagar and Ishmael in the Wilderness. Image credit: Andrea Sacchi. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The woman supports the child while the angel’s gesture directs attention outward. Hands and glances connect the close bodily crisis to another part of the landscape. The curving group fits the shaped canvas, keeping the figures related even as their attention begins to move beyond the suffering pair.

works.title: The Sacrifice of Jephthah’s Daughter
works.credit: John Everett Millais. Sacrifice of Jephthah’s Daughter. Image credit: John Everett Millais. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The embracing young woman and seated armed man establish affectionate contact, but the biblical story gives that meeting a fatal consequence. The surrounding responses prevent the embrace from being read in isolation. Millais makes the encounter difficult through the gap between a visible gesture of welcome and knowledge of the vow that burdens it.

works.title: Fair Rosamund, Study
works.credit: John William Waterhouse. Fair Rosamund (study). Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The woman’s attention passes toward the window, but its destination is withheld. Patterned textile, tiled floor and surrounding decoration make the interior more available than whatever lies outside. The study gives waiting a direction without resolving its object, keeping the figure’s look in tension with the room that contains her.

works.title: Richard Wilson
works.credit: Anton Raphael Mengs. Richard Wilson. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/anton-raphael-mengs/richard-wilson-1752
works.description: Palette and brushes identify Wilson’s occupation without requiring a studio full of supporting evidence. The soft cap and turned face keep the encounter close, while warm clothing separates him from the greenish ground. Mengs gives professional identity a modest physical form: the tools remain at hand rather than becoming a theatrical display.

works.title: Crossing the Sands to Swansea Market
works.catalogueTitle: Crossing the Sands to Swansea Market
works.credit: Edward Francis Drew Pritchard. Crossing the Sands to Swansea Market. Image credit: Edward Francis Drew Pritchard; Source credit: Art UK. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The procession of people and cattle is small in relation to the shore it crosses. The market named in the title gives the movement a destination, while water, boats and broad sky keep that purpose within a tidal landscape. Trade has a distance to travel, not merely a place of sale.

works.title: Board School Children
works.credit: Barnett Samuel Marks. Board School Children. Image credit: Barnett Samuel Marks; Source credit: Art UK. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The children occupy a shared classroom without sharing a single state of attention. Books, turned faces and hands distinguish reading, waiting and looking elsewhere. Benches hold the group together, but do not erase those differences. Marks makes schooling visible as a situation lived by several bodies rather than one idealised pupil.

works.title: Griffith Owen, Harpist to the Corbet Family
works.catalogueTitle: Griffith Owen (1750–1833), Harpist to the Corbet Family of Ynysymaengwyn
works.credit: Benjamin Marshall. Griffith Owen (1750–1833), Harpist to the Corbet Family of Ynysymaengwyn. Image credit: Benjamin Marshall; Source credit: Art UK. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The harp’s curved structure rises above and around its player, giving his profession a substantial place in the portrait. A hand near the strings indicates a practical relationship without requiring a performance to be in progress. The instrument is both identifying object and compositional partner, shaping how the figure occupies the space.

works.title: The Bal Maidens
works.credit: Emily Mary Osborn. The Bal Maidens. Image credit: Emily Mary Osborn; Source credit: Art UK :  entry 160807. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The loads make work visible through the women’s posture even as they walk away from a workplace. Aprons and head coverings distinguish individuals within their shared forward movement. Osborn keeps the group together without making the three women copies of one type: carrying is a common condition, not a complete personal identity.

works.title: Girl in a Field
works.credit: George Clausen. Girl in a Field. Image credit: George Clausen. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The girl sits low enough for the grass and its broken light to surround her. Her comparatively still figure remains distinct without being cut off from the field’s loose marks. Clausen allows person and setting to receive a related treatment, making outdoor light something shared rather than a background effect.

works.title: Cilgerran Castle
works.credit: William Havell. Cilgerran Castle. Image credit: William Havell; Source credit: Art UK. Wikimedia Commons. Public domain (https://creativecommons.org/publicdomain/mark/1.0/). Resized and JPEG-compressed; selected source frame preserved.
works.description: The castle is approached along the river, through wooded banks and shadowed foreground boats. Its height becomes intelligible in relation to that lower route. Havell lets historical architecture belong to the terrain around it instead of giving the monument a separate, unobstructed stage.

works.title: Pozzuoli
works.credit: Penry Williams. Pozzuoli. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/penry-williams/pozzuoli-1831
works.description: Animals and rough ground give the near slope a texture distinct from the broad water beyond. Buildings along the far shore establish a settlement without closing the bay. Williams makes the coastal prospect depend on this change of scale: close things require separate attention, while distance can be held together in larger areas.

works.title: Sgwd yr Henryd, Vale of Neath
works.catalogueTitle: Sgwd yr Henryd, Vale of Neath
works.credit: Penry Williams. Sgwd yr Henryd, Vale of Neath. WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/penry-williams/sgwd-yr-henryd-vale-of-neath-1819
works.description: The waterfall’s pale descent is sharply distinguished from dark rock and vegetation. The narrow space reinforces the downward direction, giving the water little room to spread sideways. Williams relies on that difference in light to establish the fall’s course while the enclosing cliff gives it height.

works.title: Mass for the Reapers
works.credit: Penry Williams. Mass for the Reapers. Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The chapel is modest beside the gathering around it. Bright clothing, resting bodies and the surrounding fields connect observance to the agricultural day. The group does not leave work’s landscape for a monumental church interior; the religious occasion takes its place within the ground and time of the reapers.

works.title: Innocents and Card Sharpers
works.catalogueTitle: Innocents and Card Sharpers (A Game of Piquet)
works.credit: Ernest Meissonier. Innocents and Card Sharpers (A Game of Piquet). Image: WikiArt. Public domain (WikiArt label). Proportionally resized and JPEG compressed; no crop.
works.description: The players watch cards and one another at close range, with little space left between hats, hands and faces. The title establishes deception, but its progress has to be read through unequal attention. Meissonier makes looking part of the contest, rather than offering the spectator a single large gesture that explains everything.

works.title: La Parisienne
works.credit: Pierre-Auguste Renoir. La Parisienne ("The Blue Lady"). WikiArt source label: Public domain. Proportional resize and JPEG compression; no crop. Source: https://www.wikiart.org/en/pierre-auguste-renoir/la-parisienne-the-blue-lady
works.description: The blue dress and matching hat give the standing woman a public presence while the setting remains lightly stated. Small shifts of light distinguish parts of the costume without breaking its overall shape. Her gloved hands supply a contained action near the waist, holding the figure together without an elaborate surrounding narrative.

closingSections.title: Follow a task through its setting
paragraphs: Compare the crossing to Swansea market with the bal maidens’ loads and the harpist’s instrument. Each makes work visible through a different relation between body and surroundings. The catalogue includes works that may be in store; consult current Museum Wales information before treating this selection as a visit plan.
